utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. And good afternoon, everyone. Could you call the case, please, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Haynes. I think that's about it. Prosecution, we have present Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Nicholls and Mr. Thayer. I understand, Mr. Zivanovic, that you have what has been described to us as a small preliminary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Everything is relative actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I just like to inform Trial Chamber and parties that we have just two more witnesses for this week. It is likely that it both of them could complete their testimonies today. Our inability to fill the gap derives from some administrative visa problems, lack of translation of two reports of our experts and for most reduced estimates both for examination-in-chief and cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand you to say that two, which means Zoran Radosavljevic and Drago Cvoric and not counting --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and not counting also Mr. Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not counting Mr. Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For those two we had 3 and a half and 3 and a half hours, six -- seven hours. By how much have their time been reduced? By how much?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that our direct will last for at least one hour for each of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's two hours. And Prosecution, I can only -- I haven't got it up here. And Prosecution, how much time do you estimate? Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. I think for Mr. Radosavljevic, we may have reduced it to about 20 minutes for cross. For Mr. Cvoric I think we are at about an hour to an hour and a half but it may be significantly less, depending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go and then we'll see. Then we'll see. But in any case, thank you for informing us, and what we would like you to avoid, all of you, in the future is indicating a time for the in chief, for the direct, and for cross which in your heart of hearts you know will probably be unrealistic. I can understand that tactically, sometimes it pays you to ask for more in case you need that time. I can understand that. But on the other hand, it creates problems. Because it has happened with each and every witness that we have had so far. And please don't forget that we have got responsibilities. Anyway, let's start and see where we get. Let's bring in Mr. Bjelanovic, please. How much more time do you have to finish with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think less than ten minutes, Your Honour, maybe five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon to you, Mr. Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, we are going to continue with your testimony today. Mr. Nicholls will take it up from where he left it yesterday and then we see whether we have further questions for you. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we have 197 up, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm going to show you now is a Drina Corps vehicle log for the month of July 1995, 1st to the 31st of July 1995. If we could start with page 1. Now, this is for a Golf, and you can see there, Witness, that we have the rank and full name of driver/user in the first box, and there we have Dusan Vucetic as driver and Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic as the user, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you didn't remember the colour of the Golf that Popovic used during this period. If I remind you that it was blue in colour, does that help you remember, dark blue?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a white Golf and a blue Golf in the Drina Corps. I can't remember exactly which he was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, my attention has been drawn by my colleague, Judge Kwon, that the 65 ter number relative to this witness is missing from the transcript, if you could -- if you could mention it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Thank you, Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Does this help you remember? As we can see right on this document that Dusan Vucetic was assigned to drive Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is again misrepresentation of the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelanovic, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask you to remove your headphones for a while, please? Can you be more specific, Mr. Zivanovic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document just shows who drove this car in month of July, not who was driver to whom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the top of the page, I don't know, I will let Mr. Nicholls answer that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the document speaks for itself. I'm using it to try to remind the witness. It says in my translation, rank and full name of driver/user.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what we have in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in Serbian it is in Cyrillic so I don't know. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is said in B/C/S [interpretation] "Driver/operator" rather than user.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Anyway, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to comment on that. Obviously, I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's go to page 2, please, of the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. But according to, operator in relation to a car would be who? Who would be the operator?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Both of them could drive this car. It means that it doesn't show that Mr. Vucetic drove Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a dash, not a slash there. That's okay. Okay. Thank you for your observation. He can put on -- yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In any event, Witness, having seen this document, does it spark your memory at all as to whether Vucetic was driving Popovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the document goes, it would seem so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page -- let's go to page -- let's leave it. I'm done with that document. Thank you. Now, different topic. You talked yesterday about the timing of the handover ceremony and you said it was around noon or a little after; remember that?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around noon. I don't remember exactly but I think it was around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You don't remember exactly. I want to see if I can help you remember. There has been a lot of evidence about the time of that ceremony. For example, Mladic was at the ceremony, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We have evidence in this case that at around 1400 hours, Mladic was in -- at Sandici meadow giving a speech to Muslim prisoners. That's from P 02853, pages 58 to 59 in the English, that's a statement of Mr. Borovcanin. So we know Mladic at 2 p.m. was far away from Vlasenica. There is another witness, PW-109, who was with Krstic all day that day of the ceremony and he recalls arriving at Vlasenica at around 1800 hours and the ceremony commencing thereafter. Now, this is July, it stays light late. Think carefully. That ceremony was in the evening, wasn't it? It's possible?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely, after so much time. In any case, I know it was that day. I know it was in Vlasenica. As for the morning or the afternoon, I don't know. I thought it was around noon. I can't tell you anything else precisely. I can provide an additional explanation by your leave concerning what I said yesterday. I made a mistake concerning my arrival in Vlasenica and concerning Vlasenica itself. It has to do with the date you asked me about. I felt a bit under pressure and I didn't provide you with the accuratest of information. I can't remember, after so much time, whether it was in the afternoon or in the morning. A lot of years have gone by. I cannot remember -- I can remember it was during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk very briefly about the next day, which is the day you went to Zepa, okay? And you say you saw Popovic there in the morning. Again, there is a lot of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic. Sorry, Mr. Nicholls. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a misstatement. The witness has never said that he saw Popovic in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll have to check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But in any event, the next day you stated that you saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- that you saw Popovic at Zepa. We have in this case, as with the ceremony, a lot of evidence, some of it uncontested, by Mr. Popovic's counsel, that on that day, Popovic, in the afternoon, in the morning around noon and into the afternoon, led a convoy of prisoners from Bratunac through Konjevic Polje towards Zvornik and then to the Orahovac school. We have other witnesses who on that day, in the afternoon -- the first Witness was PW-138 at transcript reference 3837 to 3851, another witness saw Popovic there in the afternoon about an hour after the prisoners arrived. This is the same day you were in Zepa. You've had problems with dates and times. I want you to think carefully. You were in Zepa for a long time. You saw Popovic on a different day, didn't you, not that first day that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see Mr. Popovic in Zepa. It was before Zepa, at the IKM. In Zepa, at the time, it was the Muslims who were there, their forces. We were not in Zepa at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're right. I misspoke. I'm talking about the time you say you saw Popovic at the IKM. That wasn't the first day you arrived because we know he was in Orahovac that day. You made a mistake about that, didn't you? Maybe you saw him at the IKM a different day.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely whether it was on the first or the second day but I did see him when I arrived at the IKM. Whether it was that day, the first day, or the second day, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nothing further now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Is there re-examination, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just one short question to the witness. And I'd like to show him one document. It is not at our Rule 65 ter list but it arises from the cross-examination of the witness and documents shown to him regarding Hotel Fontana and his staying at the Hotel Fontana. I'd like the usher to show it to the witness this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Is it in e-court? It's not in e-court, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's not in either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we know what it is, Your Honour? We haven't had any notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Let's -- we'll see it soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I just ask if there is a translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a translation of it, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have not had this document translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was looking at the document. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, since it a short document and I can't read it, I was wonder if we could have the interpreters just read it out so I know what it is before the questions are asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The way we do it is Mr. Zivanovic will read it out and the interpreters will translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The header says VP military post 7042 Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelanovic, could you please tell us what does VP stand for?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means military post, 7042 Bratunac. That is the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Date, the 11th of July 1995. Then HUTRO Podrinje, Hotel Fontana, Bratunac. The below-mentioned persons are granted permission to make use of a room in the Fontana Hotel between the 11th and the 13th of July 1995. Under number 1, Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic from Vlasenica. Total number of people on the list, 1. Signed by commander Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic. Have I read it out correctly?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us briefly, according to this document, since you cannot know that, but according to the document, can we conclude that Mr. Popovic was granted permission to stay in the hotel between the 11th and the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelanovic, we've come to the end of your testimony. I wish to thank you on behalf of everyone of the Trial Chamber for having come over to give testimony here and I also wish you a safe journey back home. Our staff will now give you the assistance you require to return home at the earliest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not even this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll give this exhibit, sorry. But I have no -- I have no still number of 1D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah but you intend --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to? So it's marked for identification until properly translated and you will give it a number, Madam. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We want that exhibit to come in but I would like -- it's not on his 65 ter list. I'm assuming this is one of the documents from the Hotel Fontana that Pero Mijatovic talked about that they -- during his direct, which is not on their 65 ter list. Is that where this is from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be from the army. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: These documents are not at our Rule 65 ter list, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. Where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the investigation of our investigator, Mr. Pero Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but is it part of the documents he recovered from Hotel Fontana or is it part of the documents he recovered from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. No objection. So admitted and marked for identification, as we said. Do you have any documents yourself, Mr. Nicholls, for tendering?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 -- some of the documents are already in that I used. The ones -- the now ones which should go in are 65 ter 197, 3398, and 3399.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Other Defence teams? No objection? And these are all translated, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, 3399 is not translated. That should be marked for identification. Sorry, that's the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can I have one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, regarding Mr. Zivanovic's exhibit, we can see that that is relevant material. Mr. McCloskey made an oral motion for access to that. We will be pursuing that. I would like an order that that material seized from the Hotel Fontana be kept, not be destroyed or given away and that it be kept by the Defence team until the issue of whether or not we should have access to it has been resolved, so that were we to prevail on that motion, it wouldn't be frustrated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no original of these documents at all. I just have copies, but of course, I'll not destroy it. It's in my interest to keep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there should be a measure of control. This is what Mr. Nicholls is actually suggesting or aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would request an order, Judge, formally because it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want it formally, please then formulate it formally in writing because I think it requires more attention than just a few --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand. I just mean all I would request now is an oral order formally that the material be preserved, whether it's originals, copies, whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: My only observation is where is the power, say the Prosecution, for the Trial Chamber to make the order requested. The Trial Chamber may have the power but perhaps we could be directed to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Under 54 we can always issue an injunction. So Mr. Zivanovic, yes, do you wish to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, thank you, I have said everything that I want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Then you are being instructed by the Trial Chamber not to destroy any of these documents or dispose of any of these documents until further orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next witness, Zoran Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're here to give evidence, you've been summoned for that purpose by the Defence team of Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Before you start your testimony, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration that's equivalent to an oath, that you will be testifying the truth. Madam Usher is going to hand you the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that will be your undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going to be asked a series of questions, first by the Defence team that summoned you and later on we see who will be cross-examining you. Mr. Zivanovic, if you could introduce yourself with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Radosavljevic, my name is Zoran Zivanovic. I would kindly ask you to state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us your age?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was born in 1957, in Loznica. I'm 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about your educational background?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary, secondary and higher education, and I am a lawyer by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, where do you currently reside and since when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of May 1957 in Loznica, but I reside in Donja Pilica in Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Since I was born. I have never moved out of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you serve in the army?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not. I never served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: For health reasons. I had a kidney surgery before my time came to be conscripted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And during the war, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was in my family house, with my family. That's where I lived. I didn't go anywhere from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the location of your family house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My family house is 100 metres from the culture hall in Pilica, in the very centre of Donja Pilica, on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this in the direction of Bijeljina or in the direction of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It is on the Bijeljina-Zvornik road, on the main road. My house is right there on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say a hundred metres from the culture hall, is it towards Zvornik or towards Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As you go from Bijeljina towards Zvornik. I apologise. My house is before the culture hall, so from my house you go towards the centre and it is a hundred metres from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether during the war, certain detainees were brought to Pilica and when was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, there was one group and they were there for a very short time, and I suppose that they were exchanged after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And were there any detainees after that, after 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There were some in 1995 but I learned about that only subsequently from my father. He told me that that happened because on that particular date, I wasn't there. I only heard it subsequently from my father that they were housed in the cultural hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of some detainees who were not housed in the culture hall but elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The detainees were kept in the elementary school near Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you learn about the last group of detainees?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, I was working in a company in Serbia, and I commuted to Loznica every day. On the 14th of July, when I returned home, and my house also houses a pub which is run by my parents, Petrovic Pero and Cviko Milovanovic were waiting for me there and they suggested that we should go to the elementary school because they had heard that some people had been brought there. Shall I continue? On that day, on the 14th of July, I returned home around 6.00 and I found the two of them waiting for me. After we had had a drink and after I had dinner, they suggested that together with the two of them I should go to the elementary school. We went there, the three of us, in my car, and on that day, in front of the elementary school, near Kula, I found several buses, and on those buses there were people seated, and the buses were on the road from Pilica to Bare but they were facing Zvornik. I did not linger there too long, maybe 15 or 20 minutes all together, because I saw some soldiers there whom I didn't know. In other words, I did not know any of those soldiers who were present there. I came to -- up to some 30 metres away from the school. I couldn't go any further because of the buses that were on the road, and from that distance of 30 metres, I could see about ten buses. There were not more than ten and not less than seven. I did not count them but according to my estimate, that was the number of the buses that I saw on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to clarify a few things. First you mentioned two men, Pero Petrovic and Cviko Milovanovic. Who was Pero Petrovic, whom you mentioned as one of the persons waiting for you in that pub of yours?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Pero Petrovic was the president of the commission for war conditions. Since our president Diko Micic, who was elected by people had left the area and went abroad, his position was filled by Pero Petrovic but nobody ever elected Pero Petrovic. He was just appointed to be the president of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And who was Cviko Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: At the time he was the local postman. His office was next to Pero Petrovic's office, and they socialised during the war years. Every morning they would have coffee together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were those two offices?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The offices of the local commune and the local post office are next door to each other within the premises of the culture hall or the youth hall, whatever you want to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what would be the distance between the Kula school, where you went, from the pub, from your house, that is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The elementary school is three kilometres away from Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in front of the school you saw a certain number of buses. Could you please give me some more details?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls? Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We all look alike, I know, Mr. President. The -- I just wanted to correct something I think I see for the record. The question was, can you please tell me what would be the distance between the Kula school from the pub, and his answer was the elementary school is three kilometres away from Kula. I just think that calls for some clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. It's his answer that is not clear. It wasn't your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was as follows: What is the distance between your pub where you had met with the two men from the school in Kula?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: From my house to the elementary school, the distance is 3 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please describe in some more detail those people whom you saw on the buses that were parked in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could notice, there were as many people on the buses as could be seated. I could not see anybody standing. The buses were not overcrowded. Everybody had a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Among the people on the buses, were there any children?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. There were just people whose ages ranged between 20 and 70, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they were only men?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only men. I did not notice a single woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was your impression or, rather, what was your view of the reason for these buses being there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The buses were in such a position that it seemed to me that they were ready to leave any moment. Everybody was seated. Nobody was getting off those buses. So my impression was that they were getting ready to leave any moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- did you ever enter the school in Kula, not only on that day but any time before? Are you aware of the layout of the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I completed the elementary education in that school, and I'm very familiar with the layout of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you were some 30 metres away from school. Did you see anybody in the school from that position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: From the position where I was, I could not see anybody in the school itself. The school is above the road on an elevation above the road, so from the position where I was standing, I could not see any better.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see the windows of the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What rooms could you see?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: You could see both floors, the ground floor and the first floor. You could see the windows but you could not see the inside of the class rooms in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the windows, did you see any people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. On that occasion, I did not see a single person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were the windows opened or closed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They were closed. It was during the school break. There were no students there so the school was closed. There was no need for the school to be open.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you enter the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. Not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about your two friends with whom you had come? Did they enter the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as Cviko Milovanovic is concerned, he was standing together with me. And Pero Petrovic went somewhere and I can't be sure of where he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that I was there no longer than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you leave the place on your own or did you leave with the other two?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: A bit later, before I left, Pero Petrovic returned and told us that he was supposed to make coffee or tea for the troops and that I was free to go. So I turned around together with Cviko and we went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I went home, to my family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you spend the night there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes, with my family. The following day was weekend. I was off work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So how long did you stay at home?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Until the 15th around noon. A courier came, his name is Bosko Ostojic, he was sent by Pero Petrovic, asking me to come and guard the elementary school. He told me on that occasion to get myself a gun, a rifle, and to report at the school and to guard the school. Since I was not a military conscript, I did not see it necessary for me to obey that order. I got into the car and I went to Loznica. So I did not obey that order. I did not respond to that invitation, in other words. I called my family from Loznica asking them to join me, and then I left Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Loznica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Until the end of the month, some 16 or 17 days. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your house in Pilica, did you have a telephone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you use it? Was it working at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The telephone was installed in 1988 and it worked with some minor interruptions when there was no electricity but throughout the war, it functioned and I was paying my subscription all the time. On the day when I went to Serbia, I called my wife asking her to get ready to take some money and some necessities and asked her to join me because we would be leaving from Loznica and I remember that that telephone was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So your family left at the same time as you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. My family joined me a bit later. I called my wife from Loznica. I sent a relative of mine to fetch them in a car, and then they returned together, they joined me, in Loznica, and from there we went further on to Vrnjacka Banja but that was on the same day, on the 15th. We were joined on the same day and we went further afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Pero Petrovic, as the president of the local commune or the president of that commission, as you called him, did he have any authority to issue any orders to you to the effect that you should come and guard the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what his authorities were but I am sure that he could issue orders since he had a courier, and it was my belief that I was not supposed to obey any orders from him because I was not a military conscript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have any weapons. I was never issued with any military weapons because I was never a military conscript so a rifle was never issued to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he give you any idea as to how you were supposed to guard the school, since you were not a military conscript, you did not have any military equipment, no weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose he would have given it to me if I had responded to the call but since I never did, I don't know how to answer your question. I don't know how I was supposed to guard the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you know that next to the school in Kula there were also some other prisoners in the culture hall in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: On the day when I left, I didn't know. However, when I returned, my father told me that he had bought bread and taken it to that place. Either on the day when I left or the day after. That's how I learned that the prisoners were also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever find out when it was exactly when the prisoners had been brought to the school in Kula, at what time of day? You mentioned the date but do you also have any information from any party or side as to when it was that they arrived, what time of day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard it on the 14th from Pero that they had arrived, and when I returned, I heard that they had arrived on the 14th and that some buses had lost their way and missed Pilica and only returned only two hours later. I heard that only later on, that there were buses that had missed Pilica and went in the direction of Bijeljina and returned an hour or two hours later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "miss," was that somebody's estimate that they missed their target or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that they must have had a destination and that they missed it since they went further afield and then returned to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear later on that somebody had guarded the prisoners? Did you learn of anybody guarding the prisoners, either in the culture hall or in the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: When I returned, I heard that the prisoners had been guarded by people from Srebrenica or Bratunac. In any case, it was the case of people from other areas, because I did not recognise any of the troops that I saw in front of the school. Those people had come from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And later on, did you learn from somebody, from a source of any kind, about somebody whom you know who participated in the guarding of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Recently, I've learned from my former teacher, Rajko Babic. I was surprised to hear that it was him together with some two or three elderly men who were in the school and that they were in charge of installing order. He even told me that there was no electricity, that there were no problems however but he told me only recently and I was really surprised to hear that he was in the school with these two other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you in which room those prisoners were placed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He said that, first, they were placed in the hall but because of the heat they were transferred to the classrooms, probably so that they could breathe more easily and to have more space, and of course it was easier to guard them that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you lived in Pilica for a long time, did you hear that some prisoners were killed in Pilica or in its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: When I returned from Serbia, after being away for 15 or 16 days, I heard that some people were taken to Branjevo and executed there. Of course, that's only what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the distance between the Kula school and Branjevo or the place where the prisoners were executed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I never measured it but it shouldn't be more than four and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During that time, how could one get from the Kula school to the Branjevo farm?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Then, as now, one could use two roads. There is an old road between the school and Branjevo, which is in a rather poor condition and difficult to navigate, and then there is another road which is a tarmac road. It is somewhat longer in distance but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We heard a piece of information according to which the distance between the Kula school and the place where they were shot, that is Branjevo, should be some ten kilometres. Having heard that, would you still stand by what you said, since you did not measure the distance precisely?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It cannot be ten kilometres. That would be twice the distance, 4.5 times 2, and even then it would be 9 kilometres. I was born there and I grew up there. Daily, for years, I moved about the area, and it could not be ten kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to look at some maps depicting the Kula school and Branjevo. Please have a look at those and I would kindly ask to you identify the main features. It is 1D1106. There is a small problem. The original of this map bears road markings in different colours but here we cannot see it at all. Could we please place a hard copy on the ELMO, since we can then see the colours? Could we please go down so that we could see the title? Go up, then. Yes. Could you please read out the title?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: "Pilica 12, Sepak 2, cadastre region Pilica 12, Sepak 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please zoom in on the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It will be difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you will be able to read from the screen.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The length of the old road, that was the first item. The second item, the length of the new road. And the third item is the length at which the new road towards Zvornik and Bijeljina branches off to the old road between Zvornik and Bijeljina in the length of 90 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that the blue is the length the old road between Zvornik and Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And it reads that it's 720 metres there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Then we have the distance --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The new road, Zvornik-Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The distance being?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The third --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe the third item is brown or yellowish.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The distance from the point where the old road joins the new road in the distance of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see any features there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I can indicate, if it is of any help. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is the hall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. I refrained. I was very patient. But the interpreters have been drawing your attention all along that you've been overlapping. Please, please allow one to finish and have the interpreters finish their job before you proceed with your next question or answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, take a look on previous page and check whether there is anything missing in particular in relation to distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The shortest distance is not marked on the map that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what the distance is of the shortcut in yellow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The shortcut is 90 metres from the main road, the new road, as it joins the old road, it's just this part here. It's not the complete old road, the dirt road. This is a shortcut. The complete road would be in this area. And I don't have any pencils with me to indicate it. Maybe a pointer would do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please put it in a circle.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I can indicate this portion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, would the speakers not overlap? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, please, please, please, please. Mr. Radosavljevic, before you start speaking, allow a short pause because what Mr. Zivanovic would be saying has to be translated to us into English and French. If you speak while the translation is still going on, the interpreters cannot catch up with you. So allow a short interval of time, a short pause, between question and answer, both of you, and the same applies to you Mr. Zivanovic, because you're doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll be careful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You said so a minute and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, there marking of yours, would you place 1 next to it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you next to indicate the side road, the dirt road marked in blue, and place 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Next, the asphalt road. Mark it with a 3.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, can you see where the farm at Branjevo is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked it with a 4.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the school in Kula on the map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't but I see the road leading to it. Here it is. That would be 5, if you want me to mark it. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please do so and place an arrow pointing in the direction of the school.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at something else next. The next map is 1D1107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I take it that we have finished with this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then he needs to sign it and date it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please sign the map.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, can you indicate where the hall in Pilica is? Place a 6 next to it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please sign the map and indicate today's date. Anywhere.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: What is the date today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 11th of June.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is another map. On it, can you see the intersection where the two roads branch, the dirt road and the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark that with a 1.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm placing number 1 next to the asphalt road. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I see you're putting the number 2 next to the dirt road.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, can you see the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please could we see the upper right-hand side corner? Does it say anything there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Janja. Sheet of detail, 6 K 21-B 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please sign the map and indicate today's date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record is this map 1D1107?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps to save a couple of cross questions while we have this map up, if could did I ask a little information about relative dates of production of these two maps. I just noticed on 1106 we could see the housing development plots that were put on the Branjevo farm area. The second map 1107 doesn't indicate that nor does it indicate one of the roads which had been pointed out by the witness when he was referring to 1106, so if we could just have that information, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic? I suppose you can put the questions yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the date is at the bottom of these maps. There is -- I can't see it right now. I'll check it, Your Honour. I cannot say it right now. It is aerial -- it is aerial from 1961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it from the cadastre or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it from the cadastre or not? Because it if it is from the cadastre, it has to be dated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the original from land registry or from B and H and it has the stamp of this institution but I cannot see the date, the exact dates. I have to check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can do nothing about it right now, Mr. Thayer. It has to be checked and then Mr. Zivanovic will let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 1D1108. That's another map. Can we look at the upper right corner? There is a text there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Cadastre municipality Pilica, Kula, Pilica, 2007, 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What colour is that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It is orange.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The length of the old macadam road, Bijeljina Zvornik, 460 metres so under number 2, this is 460, the length of the new Zvornik-Bijeljina road, 600 metres. Under 3, 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Kindly look at the map to see whether you can see the Kula school there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, could we zoom up the bottom part, which says stereo photo, something like that, 1961, GOD. What does it mean, the left part? The bottom part. The stereo photo, we can zoom up using the e-court, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: These are data from 1961, as far as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are these roads and everything you have marked, did they exist in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the school in Kula, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You put number 1 next to it, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you please sign this map as well and put today's date on it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radosavljevic. I have no further questions for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Now let's do the round. Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. President, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer? Do you want to break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm prepared to proceed but maybe if we broke a little early I could whittle down the cross further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Break is in seven minutes' time in any case. Break, 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My name is Nelson Thayer and I'll be asking you just a few questions on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You recall testifying as a Defence witness in the Blagojevic and Jokic case, do you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall testifying that on the 14th of July, when you had you encountered Pero Petrovic, that he told you, I think as you testified today, that he didn't have all the information about what was going to happen with these prisoners that were supposed to be coming to the school but that he'd heard something from a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember. When I arrived home around 6.00 in the evening, he told me that he had heard some people had been brought in but he didn't know what was going on and that's why he asked me to take him there, to the school. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And so my question to you, sir, is: Do you recall what he said about this conversation he had with this woman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know what the conversation was about. She was not there. She -- he only said, "I heard from some woman that some people had been brought there. Shall we go to the school?" And I said, "Yes, sure."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you got to the school, you testified today that there were troops there, soldiers. Do you recall anything particular about the uniforms that they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There was nothing extraordinary. They wore normal uniforms that were customary at the time. The only thing that I remember is that I did not recognise any single person. There was nothing else out of the ordinary that I noticed on those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about the belts they were wearing, sir? Do you recall anything in particular about the belts that some of those soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I already told at other cases that I may have noticed one white belt, but that was nothing out of the ordinary under the circumstances. Not all of them had white belts but some might have.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me just follow up on that with you. There was a question put to you, and this is at the transcript page 12059 of the Blagojevic trial and I want to be absolutely fair with you, sir. I'm just going to read the question and your answer and just tell the Trial Chamber what your best recollection is today. You testified that, "As far as I could tell and count, there were between 20 to 30 soldiers, they were not anybody I knew or had seen before." The next question was, "Were they wearing white belts?" And your answer was, "I wasn't able to see that. They were all kinds. Some were wearing the white belts and some were without." So my question is, as you sit here today, what's your best recollection as to whether or not you saw some of those soldiers wearing white belts on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As I sit here today, I hear what I said in my previous testimony and I stick to that. This is correct. It was exactly as I've already stated which means I confirm my previous words. As you know, our uniforms were of all kinds. They were not of one and the same kind. There were different kinds of armies and militaries in that area. There were some 20 or 30 soldiers whom I didn't know and they wore uniforms that were customary at the time. And that would be my answer to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified today that on the 15th of July, when the courier arrived with the instruction or order, however you want to characterise it, from Pero Petrovic, to get a weapon and proceed to the school, that you called your wife or that you first got in your car and went to your work in Serbia; is that correct? Just want to make sure I've got the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Maybe it has been misinterpreted. When Pero Petrovic's courier came to tell me that I was supposed to go and guard the school, I did not obey that order. I got into the car and I left, which means I did not respond positively to that call. I hope I made myself clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understood that part, sir. My question was, you immediately went to your place of work after getting that instruction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As soon as I got the call, I knew immediately that I wouldn't do what I was asked. I got into the car and went to Loznica. Loznica is the place where I worked. And that place is some 7 kilometres away from the place where I lived so it took me some 10 to 15 minutes to get there. And then when I was in Loznica, I used a relative's telephone to call my family who joined me an hour or two later. To answer your question, then, no, I did not respond positively to that call. I did not obey that order. I just left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified today that you told your wife and -- I believe to bring your children with her, is that correct, to meet you in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I think you have testified previously that you told her to pack things, what to bring, and you told her that you were going to be over there for some period of time; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And eventually you went to -- and forgive me pronunciation, Vrnjacka Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's in Serbia, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how far is that from Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: 250 to 300 kilometres, but I did not leave without my family. I waited for my family to rejoin me in Loznica and once they arrived, they went all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber why you disobeyed that order and gathered up your family and fled to Serbia for that period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you, I am not a military conscript. I am under no obligation to be in the army. So I did not think that I was supposed to obey Pero's order and go and guard the school with a rifle. As a sensible man, I could have expected things that would be happening in the school. As a sensible man, all I could do was to gather my family and go as far away from the school as possible. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, as a sensible man, what did you expect would be happening in the school that caused you to flee with your family and disobey that order or instruction from Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Everybody understands that on under the circumstances of war, what can be assumed if somebody tells you take a rifle and go guard somebody who is incarcerated in a school, you may expect that there would be incidents. Up to then, I never participated in any wars, in any army, and that's why I fully believe that on that particular occasion it was not my call to go and guard some school and my primary concern was for the safety of my family and my own safety. That's why I didn't go to the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, and Mr. Thayer, while the witness continued to answer the question, it transpired that we had some technical problem and that the first part of his answer is missing from the transcript. It probably was recorded but we don't have it in the transcript. So what would you like us to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can simply ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Radosavljevic, we are going to put the question again to you, for no other reason except that we had a technical problem and that the first part of your answer is missing from the transcript. So be patient with us, please, and try to answer the question. The question was, "Well, sir, as a sensible man, what did you expect would be happening in the school that caused you to flee with your family and disobey that order or instruction from Mr. Petrovic?" Could you answer the question again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I'll try. As a serious, reasonable family man, being aware of the situation, I could only assume that there might be an incident or a development that would put myself and those around me in a position to use the rifle that I might be carrying. In order to avoid any such position, in order to avoid putting myself in that position possibly, I did what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let me just read to you what your answer was to a similar question in the Blagojevic trial. This is at page 12066, beginning at line 13 of that transcript. "As Pero had told me to find a rifle and to come and guard the camp, I didn't want to get blood on my hands. I was afraid I might become a war criminal myself. And as I had managed to stay out of that up to that point, I wanted to go on like that." Isn't that the reason, sir, that you didn't want to participate in what you thought would be a mass execution of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: What I said just before the things that you're reading out to me is the same thing, only in a somewhat milder form. Of course, I expected all sorts of things could happen, even to the point of me becoming a war criminal. So what I said then, and what I said now, is one and the same thing. Only today I used a somewhat milder form of expression for what essentially is the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radosavljevic, when you got to the school and saw the troops that were in front of the school, did you see among them somebody with officer's patches, a senior officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see anybody wearing an officer's patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radosavljevic, we don't have any further questions for you, which means you're free to go. Our staff will assist you. Thank you very much for having come over to give testimony in this trial. And on behalf of everyone, may I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, any exhibits? Of course, you have the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just five maps -- three maps shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Three or more than three? How many were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe three or four. They are in e-court -- in court documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. I just renew my request to get some more information from the team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Give than we clearly see what happened after the war to that area. And that's represented in one of the maps, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We shall translate the text, at the bottom of the maps and show it to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection on the part of any of the other Defence teams? None. So these maps are admitted. I think there were -- the marked ones, but he did mark --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he marked three maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, the -- only those marked, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, the -- only those.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No exhibits from the Prosecution, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move to the next witness. How do you pronounce his name? Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm going to be leading the next witness whose name is Drago Cvoric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cvoric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Cvoric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You've been summoned as a witness for the Defence of Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Before you start your testimony, you are required under our rules to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. The text is being handed to you. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you so much. Please make yourself comfortable. You are now going to be asked a series of questions by the Defence team of Vujadin Popovic and then we see what happens next. Madam Tapuskovic, if could you introduce yourself to the witness, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, I'm going to introduce myself, my name is Mira Tapuskovic and I am a member of Mr. Vujadin Popovic's Defence team. Mr. Cvoric, since we speak the same language, in order to avoid any misunderstandings and errors in the record, I would kindly ask you to speak slowly and wait for me to finish the question before you start answering it. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Cvoric, where and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 16th of August 1947 in Dunajevic village, Zivinice municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in the -- in Republika Srpska or in the Federation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: This is in the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me something about your professional and educational background.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I am a machinist, I completed a secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you during any period of your time serve in the then JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I served my regular military duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When and where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It was in 1968 and 1969, I completed the school for reserve officers in Bileca in infantry. That was towards the end of March when I completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get a rank?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I was a Sergeant and then I went to Kosovo, Prizren, where I completed my military service and that's when I was given the rank of a second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, do you currently work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before you were retired, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: When I returned from the JNA, I was unemployed, so I joined the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the then Secretariat of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: From 15 November 1969 to the 1st of September 1991, and that's when I was retired at my own request.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, do you know Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now we will talk about the developments which took place on the eve of the war. In the first half of 1992, when war broke out, where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of May 1992, I left my house in Zivinice and I went via Tuzla and Majevica to Lopare. That's where my brother works as a policeman and I temporarily settled with him together with my wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for you to leave Zivinice, your place of residence, and go to Lopare?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The reason was the fact that the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, Muslims, started arming themselves and there was nothing for me to wait for.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And where was it that they started arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: In Zivinice.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the national composition of the place where you resided before you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: According to the last census of 1990 --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please wait for the end of my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: According to the 1991 census, there were 6 per cent Serbs, 7 per cent Croats and the rest were Muslims, and there were certain numbers of Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We are already talking about 1992. When you arrived in Lopare were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was mobilised for a month as a member of the reserve strength of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Why only a month?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I was living with my brother. His apartment was very small. There was his family, there was my wife and myself, so I looked to go somewhere else, so I went to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Under what condition did you go to Zvornik and when was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I heard it on the media that there was room for displaced persons and refugees in Zvornik, and that's why we left. And that was sometime around the beginning of July. My wife and myself went to Zvornik. We reported to the commissariat for refugees and displaced persons and they gave us accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That was in the summer of 1992. Did you then join the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please give us some details on how you joined the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
