utterances.text: After I was displaced, I took some documents with me such as my ID and my military booklet. And when we were received by the commissariat, I went to the Secretariat of National Defence and registered myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The 21st of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How come you know the date precisely?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Because in my military booklet, the date I joined the VRS was entered and also the day I left it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I have to caution you to pause and wait for the transcript. Once you joined the VRS, what was your military specialty and what was your deployment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: My military specialty is infantry. I forget what the number of the specialty is. I don't think it is important. I was deployed to the brigade command in Zvornik. I left and reported to their personnel office.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there in July 1992, tell us who was the then-commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Milutin Bosancic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was he a professional officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes. He used to be, but before the war he was retired, immediately before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said you arrived in the command of the Zvornik Brigade, what was your function, your job?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I was appointed an officer of the military security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was your position in relation to the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to the 1st Infantry Battalion in Petkovci. That's where I performed my duties for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assistant commander for security?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, for that battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What battalion was it? What was its name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It was the 1st Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us who commanded the 1st Infantry Battalion at the time of your arrival.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: At the time of my arrival, it was Captain First Class Savo Dragojlovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the 1st Battalion's command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The command was in Petkovci village. It is a local commune, in their community hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your service with the VRS, did you spend all that time with the same battalion, the same unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No. I did not stay with the battalion throughout that period. I was assigned to different battalions as was needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You told us you worked in the field of military security. In order to perform such duties, did one need certain professional knowledge in that respect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: In 1972, towards late October or early November, the Secretariat for National Defence sent me to a one-month course for a security officer to Pancevo, to the military post there. That's where I completed that course.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How is it that you remember exactly when it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: You can find that in my military booklet as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when it was that you were demobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: From the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: On the 29th of February 1996. That is in the booklet as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvoric, I would like to focus on a short interval of time, and I would kindly ask you to tell me where you were in the summer of 1992 and up to the summer next year.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: As was needed, and per brigade commander's orders, I was in several battalions. If I need to specify, I can tell you. I was with the 7th Battalion Kitovnica, then with the 10th Battalion, and by the end of 1993, I was with the 6th Battalion which was subsequently renamed the Drinjaca Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: During your service with the VRS, did you ever participate or take part in active combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, can you perhaps recall the date when Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I do. It was around the 11th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you base your recollection on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was on leave for certain reasons. My wife had a spine injury and I was given a few days of leave by the brigade commander. I believe it was a fortnight. When that took place, my commander called me on the phone and told me that Srebrenica had fallen. He called me home.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you were there all along?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: While the operation was ongoing, I was at home, assisting my wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You're trying to say that you were on leave, taking care of your wife?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasion when you were told that Srebrenica had fallen, who told you that exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Ratko [as interpreted] Petrovic, my battalion commander, he gave me a call and told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to clarify something. Page 48, line 24, Radika Petrovic. That is the battalion commander's name. During the telephone conversation, did your battalion commander give you any other information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask him if there was anything else that was new or important in relation to that event?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask him anything in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After the leave you had been given to take care of your wife, when was it that you returned again to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I believe, I cannot be precise, but it was around the 13th or the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the first day of your return as of any significance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Upon my arrival at the battalion command, we went to the front lines, we visited the soldiers, and stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say "we" went to the front lines. Could you be more specific and tell us who it was exactly? Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Battalion commander Radika Petrovic and I.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And there were no other officers with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately can you tell us what time of day it was that you went to the defence line?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: In the morning, just after I had arrived, we got ready and went there on foot, since it is a type of terrain which is not easily accessible.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your battalion command, where was the defence line in relation to the command itself? How far was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The battalion command is some 300 to 500 metres away from the defence line.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go there following an express request by your commander to visit your defence lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: We agreed on it together and we went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us whether the battalion commander, since you were absent for a number of days, advised you of any events which had taken place during your leave.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: He did. He told me that when Srebrenica fell, there was a large column of Muslim forces withdrew from Srebrenica and took the route to Jaglica Brdo, Bokcin Potok and onwards further afield.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Bokcin Potok. Tell us what the name of the place is. Does the local population have a name, a specific name, for the location where your battalion forces were at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The location is called Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there with your battalion commander, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: We set off from the right flank of our defence and we saw where those forces had gone through. Nothing was left on the patch through which they had gone through. It was almost like a runway. It was flat. There were items of clothing that had been discarded because it was extremely hot during that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you see first? Did you see your troops first or did you tour the lines? Please describe what took place that day.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: First we toured our defence line. When we were done, we went further afield to the place the forces had gone through and that is what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you first tour the soldiers along the defence lines and can you tell me whether any of the soldiers there briefed the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The company commander told us that at Bokcin Potok, there was massive firing. They could also hear horses, and the shooting lasted for a few minutes, and then it ended.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall whether the company commander, when briefing the battalion commander, specified at what time the shooting took place as well as when it was that they heard the horses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It was on the 11th -- actually, the 12th of July, around the time Srebrenica fell, when they went to Bokcin Potok ... it is very inaccessible terrain. The location is called Bokcin Potok as well as the creek there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you about the time, I meant the time of day. Were you told anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It was around -- well, in the morning hours, between 10.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember whether you were briefed on any incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to our defence line?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There had not been any incidents whatsoever, which meant that our forces didn't have any need to open fire and they did not except for one instance which involved the death of a soldier. There was nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Whose soldier was it who got killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Ours. He was a member of our battalion. It was late at night that he went out of the trench and sat on a stump. He lit a cigarette, which was clearly visible in the night. A burst of fire could be heard out of the forest, and hit him in the right upper leg. He died on the way to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this event or incident was something that the battalion commander was briefed on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown a piece of paper? Or rather, can he be given a blank piece of paper which will be placed on the ELMO? I will ask the witness to draw a sketch of the place where he toured the battalion soldiers and the rest that he's been telling us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Wait for me to tell you what you need to do. You can please sit comfortably, Mr. Cvoric. Let me go back to your testimony. You said that the defence line was a half a kilometre away from the building housing the command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: The battalion command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw the battalion command for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The square --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: This is the house where the battalion command was stationed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark that with number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You have drawn two curving lines above the battalion command. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There is a forest trail some 100 metres away from our battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place a number 2 between the two lines on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this will be the number marking the forest trail.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoric. Can you now please try and draw for us the defence line as it was positioned? The defence line of your battalion, that is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoric. Listen to me carefully now. I will be asking you to explain this sketch you drew. We want this to be entered correctly into the transcript. You have drawn a meandering line. What does that stand for? Are these elevations, hillocks or what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: These are elevations here. Where I placed the double Ts that stands for trig point. Should I place the number as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There is no need for that. On the second elevation, you've also placed the double Ts for trig point. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, between the two trig points, you've drawn several squares. Can you tell us what they stand for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: These are trenches where soldiers were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, at the time, were you shown the spot where the soldier smoking the cigarette at night was killed, was shot?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: At the -- at a trig point to the right-hand side of this one. This is where the soldier was shot, next to the trench.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place an X or a cross next to that and mark it with number 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order for us to know that the squares stand for trenches, can you place number 4 next to one of them? And that will signify that they stand for exactly that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoric. Based on the sketch you've drawn, tell us if the soldiers told you where it was that the shooting could be heard from as well as the horses neighing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes. To the right-hand side, from the spot where the soldier was shot, there was a downward slope and that was where the sounds came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a steep slope, Mr. Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was so steep as to be almost inaccessible.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoric. Please place today's date and your name in the bottom right-hand corner. It is the 11th of July today --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Of June, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have some other questions for you in relation to the sketch. I've only asked you to place your signature now because I was afraid that I might forget this later. You told us that with your battalion commander you set out to tour the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you set out on this mission on your own or were you accompanied by other people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There was just the commander and I.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us what it was that you were able to see while touring the area and can you tell us on which side of the elevations you've drawn did you see something, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: To the right-hand side of the TT trig point where the soldier was killed, some 700 to 800 metres to the right, we saw this large trail that was flattened and pieces -- and items of clothing that were discarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, this trodden trail, where did it run through? Did it run through the forest?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, through the forest all the way down to the creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw discarded items of clothing along the trail. Can you tell us how wide it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It was large, it was wide. I wouldn't be exaggerating if I said that it was as wide as a runway.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will not be needing this sketch any longer. It can be given to the Trial Chamber. Thank you, Madam Usher. Mr. Cvoric, when you were told that shooting and horses neighing could be heard out of that depression or that ditch, what did you and the commander do, if anything? Did you do anything to find out what the shooting and the neighing of the horses was all about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: At that point, we decided to take a group of -- or rather to select a group of soldiers who would go down the slope in the footprints of the column, in the footsteps of the column, to see what there was to be seen in the ditch.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long this group stayed in Bokcin Polje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: For an hour, perhaps a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed behind on that same spot, you were there as they returned from their reconnaissance mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes. We waited for them at that spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did they brief you on what they were able to see? Were you there when they briefed about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: They first radioed us, telling us that there were quite a few individuals killed down there, that there were dead horses there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, but this is something that they radioed to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When they got back, what did they tell you then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: They told us that there were many individuals who had been shot in their heads, in their chest, and that there were many horses that were killed by gunfire and many who died simply from lack of water and from sheer heat.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about the injuries that they were able to observe on the horses? Were there any weapons on the horses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were various pieces of weapons and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe the weapons yourselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: This is how it went. We ordered them to pick whatever automatic or semi-automatic rifles they could gather on the ground, these were M-48s, and to herd the horses toward the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You told us just now that they were ordered to herd the horses and take them to the battalion command. Does this mean that the horses found there were also alive, that there weren't only dead horses there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There were 23 horses that had arms mounted on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how the arms were packed, in what sort of package?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the horses had 65-millimetre shells mounted on them, which were placed in sacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I said that they had 60-millimetre mortars that were placed in sacks that had UNHCR lettering on them, and they had the globe that stood for the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, much of the territory that you have been dealing with is already included in the adjudicated facts and agreed facts. I mean, there has never been contestation on the part of the Prosecution that there was a column that a good part of it was military, that there was fighting, that there were Serbs killed in big numbers. So I don't know, I would rather concentrate on what will really help your client.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will be mindful of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, this is what I'd like to know: At the time you were at the defence lines, was there any shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told at the time that our forces had opened fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there was no shooting to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On what occasion was the fire opened, tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Only at the time of the killing of that soldier, at night. The second occasion was when one of the soldiers opened fire, made a burst of fire, that was uncalled for and we could hear -- or see in the morning that that other individual was killed too. He had a radio set by him and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did you have information about whether there had been any women or children among the dead that were found down the slope in the ditch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There were no women or children among them. They were all military-age men.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on what basis you were able to conclude that these were military-age men, conscripts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: We were able to conclude that because -- well, none of them wore uniforms, but they had military boots on their feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]? What happened to the weapons that you held over? I believe I have a problem with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the transcript is there now. Still, I would suggest that you repeat the question because as it is, it doesn't make sense. It's not your fault. It's the transcript's fault obviously. What happened to the weapons? Can you go on from there, please and repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, because of the technical error, can you please tell us what happened with the weapons that you found loaded on to the horses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: All the horses were brought to in front of the battalion command. They were unloaded. All the weapons, all the ammunition, was unloaded there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Then we informed the brigade command. We made a note of everything. A lorry was sent from the brigade command to the battalion command, to our battalion command, and that ammunition and those weapons were loaded on to the lorry and transported to the brigade command in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you ever receive information to the effect that besides the bodies of the killed person who died in that skirmish, anything was found, any piece of object, clothes or anything else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There was a lot of clothes that had been discarded. There were a lot of weapons that they had carried and there were certain pistols. I believe that all these people had licences to carry those. And there was a lot of brandy.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, was everything else made a note of and was everything else handed over to the brigade? And I'm talking about the rest of the weapons.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Everything was collected and handed over to the brigade command. No weapons were left behind lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As you were leaving the defence line, what was going on at the time? Where did you go? What was happening to the soldiers? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way. Upon the order of the brigade commander, we withdrew from those positions, not a single soldier remained there. We went toward Orahovac to the elementary school and we were billeted there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were the soldiers pulled over the same day when you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of us went. Nobody was left behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So nobody was left behind then. Did you hear on that occasion, in any of the conversations with your commander, or the other soldiers, that an order had been issued to use weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: There was no need for that, so no such thing was ever issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you what happened to the defence line, since you've told us that all the soldiers were recalled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Everything was free, there was no need for anybody to remain there. Everything was clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. One moment. Mr. Ostojic, you ever indicated that you don't wish to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Pandurevic has already signified. You confirm that, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good evening to you. I may have a few questions. I'd appreciate it if we could take the break now and I think it will be a lot shorter than I anticipated originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cvoric.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My name is Kweku Vanderpuye, I'm an attorney with the Prosecution. I'm going to put some questions to you in relation to your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you going to finish today or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I anticipate that I'll finish hopefully within 15 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. No. Because if you weren't, then I would have asked you again whether you still insist that tomorrow's sitting be in the afternoon or whether we could shift it to the morning. All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to clarify something right at the beginning, Mr. Cvoric. You were a member of the 8th Battalion in July 1995, that's correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in July 1995, that battalion was actually under the command of the Bratunac Brigade as the 4th Battalion of that brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, you mentioned that you were away during the beginning part of July and when you returned you were briefed in some respects about what actually transpired over several days. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at the time you held the position of assistant commander for security and intelligence for the battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to that position, you had several responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Of course, just as in any military.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Among the responsibilities you had is that you were tasked with organising and collecting and processing data about the enemy in the area of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also had to plan and organise intelligence and security or reconnaissance in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was our job.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you also had to ensure that the gathering and forwarding of intelligence data on the enemy transpired?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just have 65 ter 3402 in e-court, please? Okay. If I could refer you -- if we could just go down the page, please, to where you see paragraph 2, we should be able to capture what I want, all the way -- all the way down? Okay. It's the second -- or the third-to-last point there. And one of the functions that you had as the assistant commander for security and intelligence was that you had to carry out necessary interrogation of war prisoners and refugees and arrange for their evacuation to a determined place. You see that written on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just scroll up to the top, please, for a moment. Way at the top. You see your name on this document, Mr. Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the top, in the right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you did mention that you were briefed on a shooting that occurred while you were away. You had mentioned that a Serb soldier who was smoking a cigarette was shot. You recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were informed that that soldier's name was Djordje Vukosavljevic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I have forgotten in the meantime but yes you're right now that you mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And were you informed that he was shot in the leg and that he bled to death on the way to the hospital, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the right upper leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information that the 1st Company of the battalion had captured Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You sure about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. I am sure that it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could have in e-court, please, 65 ter 1121, D is the English, C is the B/C/S, please, and could I ask that it not be broadcast. If we could just go, the time will be reflected on there as 1640. Okay. There we go. This is an intercept that I'm showing you that's dated 12th of July, the time is 1640. All right. And it reads, in part, the Turks -- or my guys had captured a Turk alive but unfortunately we later on and someone in the background on Obrenovic side says that's been shot, they sent him, yes they've sent him for exchange. You see that part written in this intercept, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you were never provided with any of that information from your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this because on that dates I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You aware that Radika Petrovic, your commander, testified about this particular circumstance at a prior trial, on 5 May 2004? And he said in essence between pages 8725 and 8737 of that trial that in fact the 1st Battalion did receive a captured Muslim and that the Zvornik Brigade had been informed of that and that Obrenovic had issued orders that the prisoner be taken to Kajici and that he was to be taken to an asphalt road there and collected by Dusko Vukotic. Did you receive any of that information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He also said that according to what the commander of the 1st Company told him, that they took the prisoner and that he started trying to escape and that he went toward a minefield which had trip wire mines and that their lives would have been endangered, all of their lives would have been endangered, so they shot him to death. Did you receive any of that information, Mr. Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Further on in his testimony, he actually says that Dusko Vukotic actually never went to the command because that's where he was with his security man, and that would be you, wouldn't it, Mr. Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I never met Vukotic in my battalion, never in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you met Mr. Vukotic. I'm asking you whether or not Mr. Petrovic told you about this prisoner that had been shot by members of the 1st Company of your Battalion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about a separate prisoner altogether, one that was captured on the 13th. Did your commander ever tell you about a Muslim prisoner that was captured on the 13th by this same 1st Company of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, he testified, as I said, about two incidents and this is the second one of which he testified about and what he said was that a prisoner was taken by the 1st Company of your battalion, that's the night of the 13th, the morning of the 14th, he was brought to the battalion command where he was questioned by commander Petrovic, he gave his name, and his name was Asif Gabeljic, about 45 years old and that he was interviewed or interrogated by Mr. Petrovic. Did you ever hear about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that this particular individual was turned over to one Momir Nikolic of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And would it surprise you to learn that this particular individual, we have evidence, showed up in a grave site in Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: It's possible but I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: One of your responsibilities as a security and intelligence officer is to know these kinds of things; isn't that right, Mr. Cvoric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, but before I said that during that particular period of time, I was off duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just one moment. Bear with me for one second, Your Honours, just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 317 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoric, can you see what's in front of you there on the screen? This is an attendance log --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Attendance log for your brigade. If we could just go over to your battalion, if we could just go over and see that this is for the month of July. You see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And your attendance for the days of 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, are all marked with a plus indicating that you're present at the command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I can't see the dates. What dates are --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you look on the top right-hand corner, you can see that it's for the month of July. You see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you recognise your name on that document, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're the fourth one down? I'm sorry, the third one down?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO CVORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you Mr. Cvoric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Is there re-examination, Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. We don't have any further questions for you, which means you can go. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having accepted to come and give evidence here, and on behalf of everyone present, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exhibits? Exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have any exhibits from the 65 ter list, save for the sketch that the witness himself drew during his evidence-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection to the admittance of that sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from the other Defence teams? None. So it is so admitted. Any exhibits on your part?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have two. One is 65 ter 317, which is the attendance log or attendance sheet, I should say. And then the second document is 65 ter 3402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Zivanovic? Or Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objections from the other Defence teams? None. They are so admitted. Now, these past few days, starting from the 2nd of June when we started the Defence case, has, if anything, served to teach us all or some of us a lesson, namely that the projected estimates that we have been receiving are inflated. I'm not in any way hinting that they are inflated intentionally because I've spent my life as a lawyer before I became a judge, and I know that when it comes to the Defence case, sometimes the prognosis changes from time to time. And I would expect this pattern to continue. In fact, even before -- or rather when you filed, each one of us filed your estimates and 65 ter documents, in our discussions I made it clear that this was my anticipation based on my past experience. And it is happening indeed. While it happens, it can cause damage, and this is what I would try and avoid as much as I can. I would like you again to sit down, Mr. Zivanovic, and I am not in any way criticising you. I know that you have been reasonable, you've done your work well, so don't read my message as a criticism. It's not a criticism. It's an invitation to sit down again and go through the whole exercise again. I know that today and tomorrow we can't do anything because the next witness is already scheduled to testify by videolink and you could not anticipate that we would finish with your list on Wednesday, but for the future, you need to take this into account as a -- not only a possibility but as a probability, because I can assure you this is how it's going to go on. All right? Next message is to you, Mr. Ostojic. The way I read things, your case may come up pretty much earlier than you may have anticipated. There are still a few unfinished symphonies on your desk, and if you -- which I am sure you have, you've seen the latest filing by the Prosecution in relation to 92 bis, et cetera, et cetera. There is an indication of what still needs to be done by you. We are working on that as well and we are identifying what still needs to be done by you but rather than us coming back to you and tell you what to do, when to do it and so on and so forth, I would appreciate if you take the opportunity now that you have got these two days to sit again with your team but also with the Prosecution and try to trim whatever needs trimming and file or disclose what still remains to be disclosed. There are statements. There are translations. There are quite a few things. And I wouldn't like you to find yourself unpleasantly surprised either by some intervention on our part or by a sudden stop or termination of the Popovic Defence team, which I am sure will finish earlier than we had anticipated. So for the time being I'm limiting myself to Mr. Zivanovic and to you. Yes, one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Kwon is also making a good point and a suggestion. On Monday, we have that individual testifying by videolink. The next witness is Nedjo Blagojevic, also by videolink. What I would like you to do is to make, in consultation with the Prosecution and your colleagues and the other Defence teams, a near enough best estimate possible of how long you expect the videolink of Rakic to last so that if it is anticipated to last less than the sacramental three and a half hours or three hours 45 minutes and there is a leftover, we would like to you see whether it is possible to make an arrangement for Blagojevic, Nedjo -- sorry, for Branko Bogicevic to be present here and start his evidence immediately we finish with Rakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogicevic has to come to The Hague on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it means you will have enough time to proof him and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Make your calculations exactly as to the rest of the week because, again, I mean, if we spend Monday, the whole of Monday, with Rakic, and then we have got Tuesday with Blagojevic. All right. I'm going to leave it entirely in your hands. I know that you are a very capable lawyer. But, please, try to -- I know it's difficult. I mean, it's not easy, because what happens in trials is sometimes not possible to anticipate, but I'm going to leave it in your hands, feeling 100 per cent sure of your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best to meet your requirements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. All right. We stand adjourned until Monday, Monday in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of June, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.23 p.m.,
